providers.service_territory: Most of Arizona excluding the greater Phoenix metro (SRP) and Tucson (TEP); serves 11 counties including portions of Maricopa, Yavapai, Coconino, Mohave, and others
providers.notes: Largest IOU in Arizona. APS Solutions for Business (S4B) HVAC and New Construction rebates were discontinued Jan 1 2026 per ACC Decision No. 81584; remaining S4B lighting and custom programs still active per Jan 2026 Policies & Procedures. APS filed a 2025 rate case (June 2025) with new rates expected H2 2026. Program administered by DNV.

providers.service_territory: Greater Phoenix metropolitan area; largest electricity provider in the Phoenix metro, serving approximately 1.2 million customers
providers.notes: Community-based, not-for-profit public power utility. Business program year runs May 1–April 30. Program website also accessible at savewithsrpbiz.com. FY25 program overview effective May 1, 2024–April 30, 2025.

providers.service_territory: Tucson metropolitan area and surrounding Pima County; serves approximately 440,000 customers in southern Arizona
providers.notes: Subsidiary of UNS Energy (Fortis). Business Energy Solutions program includes Commercial, Schools, Custom, and Multifamily tracks. Trade Ally contractor participation required for most rebates. Funding limited; customers encouraged to apply promptly.

providers.service_territory: Mohave County (northwestern AZ) and Santa Cruz County (southern AZ); serves more than 243,000 customers across Arizona
providers.notes: Subsidiary of Fortis Inc. UES shares a very similar Business Energy Solutions program structure with TEP (sister utility under UNS Energy). Also offers Commercial Energy Solutions and EV charger rebates for commercial customers. Efficient Home Program administered by Franklin Energy (residential). Commercial program contact: (866) 540-4315.

programs.program_name: Solutions for Business (S4B) – Existing Facilities Lighting & Controls (2026)
required_documents: W-9 if rebate paid to customer
programs.stacking_rules: No stacking of prescriptive + custom rebates for same measure; federal and state programs may be stackable separately
programs.funding_status: Open – waitlist created when annual budget is fully subscribed
programs.program_notes_ai: HVAC and New Construction rebates under S4B were discontinued effective January 1, 2026, per ACC Decision No. 81584. Lighting, controls, and remaining prescriptive measures continue under Jan 2026 Policies & Procedures. Program administered by DNV; applications submitted via apsapplynow.com. Rebate paid to contractor if contractor submits on behalf of customer. Annual budget fully distributed each program year; waitlist applies when budget is reached.

programs.program_name: Solutions for Business (S4B) – Custom / Large Facility (2026)
programs.stacking_rules: Custom measures cannot be double-counted with prescriptive rebates for the same measure
programs.program_notes_ai: Custom track requires pre-approval before project completion. Rebate feasibility studies available: capped at 50% of study cost up to $2,500 per phase (Discovery and Implementation). No rebate payments are guaranteed; each submission is reviewed for eligibility individually.

Contact MEEP team at 866-277-5605 or apsmeep@dnv.com. Includes rebates for Wi-Fi-connected electric water heaters in residential units. New Construction offering includes both prescriptive and performance tracks.

programs.program_name: Multifamily Energy Efficiency Program (MEEP) – New Construction (2026)
programs.program_notes_ai: New Construction includes rebates for pre-selected equipment (prescriptive) and energy-saving performance goals (performance approach). Energy Advisor assigned to guide project from start to finish.

programs.stacking_rules: Overall annual cap per customer is $450,000 across all SRP programs (May 1–April 30); Energy Efficiency sub-cap is $300,000; Business EV sub-cap is $300,000; Electric Technology sub-cap is $100,000. Program-level caps may also apply.
programs.program_notes_ai: Covers LED lighting, HVAC, refrigeration, motors, data centers, and more. Program year runs May 1–April 30. SRP reserves right to determine which program year a rebate is attributed to. Contact: (602) 236-3054 or businessrebates@srpnet.com. Participating contractors (Trade Allies) can guide and process rebate paperwork.

programs.program_name: Business Energy Efficiency – Small Business Solutions (FY2025)
programs.stacking_rules: Subject to overall $450,000 annual customer cap across all SRP programs; Energy Efficiency sub-cap $300,000
programs.program_notes_ai: Designed specifically for small and midsize businesses with simple upgrades to thermostats, lighting, and HVAC. Remote virtual program option available; may help reduce energy costs up to 15% without on-site visits.

programs.stacking_rules: Subject to $300,000 Energy Efficiency sub-cap and $450,000 overall annual customer cap
programs.program_notes_ai: Flexible program for unique facility improvements such as insulation, roofing, compressed air, and pumping systems. Pre-approval required before project completion. Eligible for industrial and large commercial accounts.

programs.stacking_rules: No conflict with Energy Efficiency programs; subject to separate program caps
programs.program_notes_ai: No-cost, no-risk program that pays businesses to cut energy consumption during times of high demand. Strategies include reducing nonessential lighting or adjusting HVAC settings during peak demand events.

programs.stacking_rules: Rebates capped at 75% of incremental cost per prescriptive measure; custom measure cap is 50% of incremental cost
programs.funding_status: Open – funding limited; customers encouraged to apply immediately
programs.program_notes_ai: Covers lighting, refrigeration, controls, and HVAC systems including variable speed drive air compressors ($100/HP). Must use TEP-approved Commercial Trade Ally for installation; rebate deducted from project cost at point of service. Applications submitted via tep.com/business-energy-solutions/commercial-program/application/.

required_documents: Custom Lighting Worksheet 1 (wattage reduction, no schedule change) – updated 4/22/2026
Custom Lighting Worksheet 2 (wattage reduction + schedule change) – updated 4/22/2026
Room Count Sheet (required for >30 fixtures or de-lamping)
programs.stacking_rules: Custom measures capped at 50% of incremental cost; prescriptive measures capped at 75% of incremental cost; same measure cannot receive both
programs.program_notes_ai: Pre-application required before project initiation. Worksheets updated April 2026. Only TEP customers on eligible commercial pricing plans qualify. Energy-efficient equipment purchased, contracted, or completed prior to program start date is not eligible.
Enhanced program specifically for K-12 schools with rebates for lighting, HVAC, and refrigeration. Requires TEP-approved Trade Ally contractor.
Designed for owners and managers of multi-family complexes. Cash rebates available for lighting, controls, AC, heat pump, motors, and motor drives.

programs.stacking_rules: Rebates capped at 75% of incremental cost per measure; funding limited
programs.funding_status: Open – funding limited; applications submitted for projects with reserved funds will receive original incentive amount
programs.program_notes_ai: Program structure mirrors TEP Business Energy Solutions (sister utility). Covers high-efficiency lighting, HVAC, refrigeration upgrades via approved Trade Ally contractors. Serves Mohave County and Santa Cruz County customers only. Commercial Energy Solutions program details at uesaz.com/efficiency/.
K-12 school specific track under UES Business Energy Solutions. Covers lighting, HVAC, and refrigeration via approved Trade Ally. Program structure mirrors TEP Schools program.

programs.stacking_rules: Rebates issued as bill credit on UES account; may be combined with federal IRA EV charging incentives where eligible
programs.program_notes_ai: Allows commercial customers—businesses, government agencies, public transit, nonprofit organizations, and multifamily complexes—to save on installing EV charging ports at their facilities. Serves Mohave and Santa Cruz County UES electric customers. Networked Level 2 charger rebate covers up to 75% of initial purchase cost.

rate_schedules.description: General service for small commercial customers typically under 20 kW demand; no demand charge; flat energy rate
rate_schedules.notes: ACC Decision No. 79293 effective March 8, 2024. Rate case filed June 2025; new rates expected H2 2026. Actual rates may vary with adjustors (PPFAC, REAC, LFCR).

rate_schedules.description: General service for medium commercial customers with demand component; billed demand based on highest kW or 80% of highest summer kW during trailing 12 months
rate_schedules.notes: ACC Decision No. 79293 (ACC No. 6156, Revision No. 4). Minimum monthly bill = Basic Service Charge + Bundled Demand Charge. Rate pending 2025 rate case outcome.

rate_schedules.description: Large general service with demand charge; demand billed at highest of: measured kW, 80% of highest summer kW in trailing 12 months, or contract minimum
rate_schedules.notes: ACC No. 6156, Revision No. 4, effective March 8, 2024 (Decision No. 79293). Three-phase 60 Hz service at standard available voltages.

rate_schedules.description: Time-of-use rate for extra large customers (data centers, large industrial); three-phase, 60 Hz; daily metering charges apply; specialized equipment may incur additional metering charges
rate_schedules.notes: Effective March 8, 2024. APS proposed 45%+ rate increase for extra-large energy users (e.g. data centers) in 2025 rate case. Pending ACC approval expected H2 2026.

rate_schedules.schedule_name: Service Schedule 1 – Residential / Small General Service (TOU Option)
rate_schedules.description: TOU option for small commercial/general service customers; APS proposed to revise Service Schedule 1 in 2025 rate case; peak period typically 4–7 PM weekdays
rate_schedules.notes: APS proposed revisions to Service Schedule 1 and Schedule 3 in its June 2025 rate case filing. Critical Peak Pricing riders proposed to be eliminated.

rate_schedules.description: Flat monthly per-fixture charge for street and outdoor area lighting; rate depends on fixture wattage and type
rate_schedules.notes: Per-fixture monthly billing; specific wattage-based rates available in full tariff on APS website.

rate_schedules.description: Small commercial general service for accounts under 20 kW demand; flat energy rate; no demand charge
rate_schedules.notes: SRP is a publicly owned utility not subject to ACC rate regulation; rates set by SRP Board. Contact SRP for current published tariff.

rate_schedules.description: Medium commercial general service with demand charge; typically 20–1,000 kW
rate_schedules.notes: SRP rates not subject to ACC regulation. Contact SRP for current published tariff schedule.

rate_schedules.schedule_name: E-32 – Large Power / TOU (Manage Demand 5–10 PM)
rate_schedules.description: Time-of-use demand rate for large commercial and industrial customers; on-peak period 5–10 PM; aligned with SRP's 'Manage Demand 5–10 PM and Save' price plan
rate_schedules.notes: SRP price plan branding: 'Manage Demand 5-10 p.m. and Save'. Contact SRP for official published tariff rates.

rate_schedules.description: Agricultural and irrigation pumping service for SRP customers; seasonal demand and energy charges
rate_schedules.notes: SRP also manages a large irrigation water delivery system. Contact SRP for current agricultural rate tariff.

rate_schedules.description: Small commercial general service without demand charge; for accounts typically under 20 kW
rate_schedules.notes: TEP offers four distinct small commercial plans including flat and TOU options. TEP historic average rate shown in TEP affordability tables.

rate_schedules.description: Small commercial TOU plan with discounts for off-peak usage; two of four small commercial plans include TOU rates
rate_schedules.notes: TEP offers two TOU and two demand-based small commercial plans. Customers can choose based on usage patterns.

rate_schedules.description: Small commercial demand plan that pairs reduced energy charges with a demand charge; rewards customers who can limit concurrent large appliance use during on-peak hours
rate_schedules.notes: Two of four TEP small commercial plans pair reduced energy charges with demand charge.

rate_schedules.schedule_name: TG-4 – Medium / Large Commercial Demand TOU
rate_schedules.description: Medium to large commercial TOU demand plan for accounts over 20 kW; demand-based pricing with time-of-use energy rates
rate_schedules.notes: TEP business rate plans include time-of-use and demand-based pricing options. Full tariff at tep.com/business-rates/.

rate_schedules.description: Small general service for commercial accounts without demand component; Mohave and Santa Cruz County service areas
rate_schedules.notes: UES rate case underway; PPFAC adjustment effective May 1 through December 2026. Contact UES at 1-877-837-4968 for current tariff.

rate_schedules.description: Medium commercial general service with demand charge; serves Mohave County (Kingman area) and Santa Cruz County (Nogales area)
rate_schedules.notes: UES is a Fortis subsidiary. New annual rate adjustment process initiated; see uesaz.com for current tariff details.

rate_schedules.description: Large commercial TOU demand rate for accounts over defined demand threshold in Mohave and Santa Cruz Counties
rate_schedules.notes: Contact UES at 1-877-837-4968 or visit uesaz.com for current published tariff schedule.

forms.program_name: Solutions for Business (S4B) – Existing Facilities Lighting & Controls (2026)
forms.form_notes: Online application portal for all S4B prescriptive rebates. Replaces paper application. Administered by DNV.

forms.program_name: Solutions for Business (S4B) – Existing Facilities Lighting & Controls (2026)
forms.form_notes: Full program policies and procedures document published January 2026. Covers eligibility, caps, documentation requirements, and payment processes.

forms.program_name: Solutions for Business (S4B) – Custom / Large Facility (2026)
forms.form_notes: Pre-application must be submitted and approved before project begins. Final application submitted post-completion. Online portal via apsapplynow.com.
Contact MEEP team at 866-277-5605 or apsmeep@dnv.com to initiate. Online application via same DNV portal as S4B.

forms.form_name: SRP Commercial Energy Efficiency Rebate Application
forms.form_notes: Application submitted through SRP online portal or via participating Trade Ally contractor. Contact (602) 236-3054 or businessrebates@srpnet.com. CEE Program Overview PDF available at srpnet.com/assets/srpnet/pdf/doing-business/cee-program-overview.pdf.
Pre-approval required before project initiation. Contact SRP Business Energy team at (602) 236-3054 to begin process.
Standard rebate application for TEP commercial prescriptive measures. Submitted by TEP-approved Trade Ally contractor.

forms.form_name: TEP Custom Program – Part 1: Pre-Application / Final Application
forms.form_notes: Combines Pre- and Final Application in one form. Must be completed before project initiation for pre-approval.

forms.form_name: Custom Lighting Worksheet 1 – Wattage Reduction, No Schedule Change
forms.form_notes: Required for custom lighting projects with wattage reduction and no change in operating schedule. Updated 4/22/2026.

forms.form_name: Custom Lighting Worksheet 2 – Wattage Reduction + Schedule Change
forms.form_notes: Required for custom lighting projects with both wattage reduction and operating schedule change. Updated 4/22/2026.
For custom projects that do not fit Custom Lighting Worksheet 1 or 2. Updated 4/22/2026.
Required for all lighting projects with more than 30 fixtures and all de-lamping projects.

forms.form_name: UES Commercial Energy Solutions Rebate Application
forms.form_notes: Application submitted via UES website or through an approved Trade Ally contractor. Program structure mirrors TEP Business Energy Solutions.

forms.form_name: UES Smart EV Charging Commercial Rebate Application
forms.form_notes: For businesses, government agencies, nonprofits, public transit, and multifamily complexes in Mohave and Santa Cruz Counties. Rebate issued as bill credit.
